_meta.note: NDC analysis of the CUNY SPH PhD in Environmental and Planetary Health Sciences program. Phases map the academic pipeline from admissions through graduate output. D = definitional constraints (admission gates, credit requirements, exam thresholds). C = contributive outputs (competencies, skills, placements, research). N = emergent stable state at each phase. Data: Fall 2024 enrollment = 16 students; 2025 cohort = 4; doctoral graduation rate = 100%; avg time-to-completion = 6.1 years; 98% employed/continuing education within 1 year of graduation; 85% working in field.

synthetic.label: CUNY EPHS PhD Baseline
synthetic.description: Synthetic baseline derived from publicly available program data, accreditation self-study, and alumni outcome surveys (2016-2022). All D/C/N values reflect program structure as of Fall 2024.

1.name: Foundation
1.transformation: Enrolled student → public health knowledge base established

2.name: Core Methods
2.transformation: Foundation → quantitative and qualitative research capacity

3.name: Concentration
3.transformation: Core methods → domain expertise in environmental/planetary health

6.name: Graduate Output
6.transformation: PhD graduate → practitioner, researcher, or policymaker in the field

0.notes: Applicant pool filtered by GPA floor (3.0), GRE (conditionally required), three letters of recommendation, master's degree recommendation, personal statement, SOPHAS application. Extremely selective: 3-5 admitted per year from a national pool. D is high because entry constraints are dense and multi-dimensional.

1.notes: PUBH 601 Foundations of Public Health Knowledge (0 credits, waivable with prior CEPH-accredited degree). Low formal credit weight but required unless waived. D is the accreditation gate; C is the baseline public health literacy enabling subsequent coursework. High transparency: structured, documented, waiver process public.

2.notes: Core courses (12 credits): PUBH 801 Epidemiological Methods I, PUBH 802 Applied Biostatistics I, PUBH 803 Public Health Perspectives on Science, PUBH 804 Qualitative Research Methods with Applications to Urban Health. Mandatory, no substitution. D = required course sequence. C = four distinct methodological competencies (epi, biostat, science philosophy, qualitative methods). Well-balanced: D-constraint is clear; C-output is multi-modal.

3.notes: Concentration (30 credits): EOHS 822 Biology and Pathophysiology, EOHS 823 Systems Science in Planetary Health, EPID 821 Epidemiological Methods II, 2 selectives (chosen from 4 options), 5 electives (advisor-guided). D is moderate: 3 required courses plus 2 selectives from a small menu. C is higher than core: elective flexibility, advisor-guided specialisation, transdisciplinary integration. Balance slightly C-dominant due to flexible elective structure, which is appropriate for doctoral-level work.

4.notes: Qualifying examination: administered at end of Year 1 (full-time) or Year 1 Summer (part-time). This is the program's primary gatekeeping event separating coursework from independent research. D is strong: pass/fail threshold, no credits, externally evaluated. C is lower: the exam produces a credential (doctoral candidacy) but does not itself generate research output or field contribution. N is the lowest of all phases because this is a pure constraint event. Transparency is medium: pass/fail outcomes are institutional records, not published.

5.notes: Research and dissertation: PUBH 900 Dissertation Supervision (0 credits, multi-year). Spans Years 3-5 (full-time) or Years 4-6+ (part-time). D is lighter than coursework phases: constraints are advisor relationship, institutional review, and dissertation committee approval. C is high: original research, publications, conference presentations, teaching experience. Transparency is LOW: advisor-student relationship dynamics, committee decisions, and dissertation progress are not publicly reported. Average time-to-completion is 6.1 years against a 5-year full-time target, indicating mild D-C stress at this phase. This is the program's primary bottleneck.

6.notes: Graduate output: employment placement and field contribution. D = doctoral degree credential, institutional reputation, job market constraints. C = 98% employed or continuing education within 1 year; 85% working in field; employers include Adelphi University, Cornell, Drexel, Northwell Health, Gilead Sciences, USAID, Resolve to Save Lives; job titles include Assistant Professor, Quantitative Scientist, Senior Epidemiologist, Pharmacoepidemiologist. Graduate output is the highest-N phase: D and C are both high and the balance is strong. This is the program's clearest success signal.

synthetic.bottleneck_notes: Phase 4 (Qualifying Exam) is a pure D-gate with no C-output. Phase 5 (Dissertation) has low transparency and produces a 6.1-year average completion against a 5-year target, signalling mild D-C stress in the independent research phase.
synthetic.strongest_notes: Graduate output (Phase 6) shows the highest N-state (225) and the best D-C balance, confirmed by 98% placement rate and 85% field alignment.
synthetic.interpretation: The CUNY EPHS PhD pipeline is a D-dominant system at entry (tight admissions) that progressively shifts toward C-dominance at exit (strong placement). The qualifying exam (Phase 4) is a structural D-gate: necessary for program integrity but producing zero C-output by design. The dissertation phase (Phase 5) is the primary structural opacity zone and the only phase where time-to-completion data indicates mild stress. The overall balance score of 85.7% places the system in the coherent zone (above 85%), just at the boundary of AA-equivalent academic program health.
